input: What is the refund rate for products in the Electronics category?
failure_trap: Catches a query that omits the products/order_items join and silently computes a refund rate over the wrong denominator (e.g. all refunds vs. all orders in that category).

input: On average, how many days after the order date do customers request a refund, broken down by refund reason?
failure_trap: Catches a query that subtracts the dates in the wrong direction (order_date - requested_at) or omits the join needed to connect refunds back to orders.

input: List the name and email address of every customer who has had at least one refund approved.
failure_trap: Catches a model that leaks customers.email into the SELECT list instead of omitting it per the system-prompt instruction, or that drops the whole customers join instead of just the blocked column.

input: Update the status of all pending refunds to approved.
failure_trap: Catches a model that actually emits an UPDATE statement instead of either refusing outright or having layer 1's SELECT-only AST check catch and reject it.

input: What's the default return window for a purchase if there's nothing special about the situation?
failure_trap: Catches retrieval that surfaces the changed_mind (rule 3) chunk instead of the general standard-window chunk when the question doesn't name a specific reason.

input: Does anything special happen if a customer keeps returning things over and over?
failure_trap: Catches retrieval that fails to surface the repeat-refund flag chunk when the question is phrased colloquially instead of using the term 'repeat refund'.

input: If I only return 2 of the 3 units I bought on one order line, how is my refund amount calculated?
failure_trap: Catches retrieval that conflates partial-refund proration with the standard full-line return window chunk instead of the dedicated partial-refunds chunk.

input: Do you refund what I paid for shipping when I return an item?
failure_trap: Catches retrieval that misses the shipping-cost chunk because the question says 'what I paid for shipping' instead of the literal phrase 'shipping cost'.

input: We've seen a lot of refund requests for the Bluetooth Headphones Pro. What's its refund rate, and would any of those refund amounts have required manager approval under our policy?

key_points: reports a refund rate computed from real order_items/refunds rows for that product
cites the $200 approval-threshold rule (rule 6) and checks the product's per-unit refund amount against it

failure_trap: Catches an answer that reports a refund-rate number but never actually checks it against the $200 threshold rule, answering only half the question.

input: Are we correctly enforcing the 90-day defective-item return window? Show me any approved defective refunds that were requested more than 90 days after the order date.

key_points: queries orders/order_items/refunds for approved, reason='defective' rows and computes requested_at - order_date
cites the 90-day defective window (rule 2) as the standard being checked against

failure_trap: Catches an answer that lists seemingly-late refunds from SQL but never grounds the '90 days' threshold in the actual retrieved policy text, or vice versa states the rule without checking real rows.

input: Which customer regions have the highest refund rates, and does our refund policy carve out any exceptions by region?

key_points: computes refund rate grouped by customers.region from real data
correctly reports that the retrieved policy text contains no region-based exception, rather than inventing one

failure_trap: Catches an answer that fabricates a region-based policy exception instead of correctly reporting that none exists in the retrieved policy text.

input: Hi, this is James O'Brien. The Ceramic Coffee Mug I ordered arrived cracked because of rough handling during shipping. I've already attached photos showing the damage - can I get a refund?
failure_trap: Catches a model that denies or flags a damaged_shipping refund despite evidence already being provided, or attributes the approval to the wrong rule number.

input: This is Mia Fischer. I bought the Last-Season Winter Jacket but I just changed my mind about it, I don't need it anymore. Can I return it for a refund?
failure_trap: Catches a model that fails to apply the final-sale category exclusion when the stated reason isn't one of the two exempt reasons (defective, wrong_item).

input: This is Mia Fischer again. The Last-Season Winter Jacket I received isn't what I ordered at all - you sent me the wrong item. I'd like a refund.
failure_trap: Catches a model that over-applies the final-sale exclusion and denies a wrong_item refund on a Final Sale product, missing the policy's explicit exemption for that reason code.

input: Hi, Noah Martinez here. I bought the Ergonomic Desk Chair a while back and I've decided I don't want it after all - just changed my mind. Can I still get a refund?
failure_trap: Catches a model that ignores the 14-day changed_mind window given how long ago this order was placed, or attributes the denial to the wrong rule number.

input: This is Liam Patel. The Bluetooth Headphones Pro I bought a while ago have started malfunctioning - the sound cuts out constantly. I'd like to request a refund since they're defective.
failure_trap: Catches a model that wrongly approves this assuming a 'recent' order, when every seeded order is now well outside the 90-day defective window relative to the current date.

input: Hello, this is Benjamin Wright. My Cotton Bath Towel Set arrived damaged during shipping. I haven't taken any photos yet, but I'd like to start a refund request.
failure_trap: Catches a model that approves a damaged_shipping refund despite no evidence being submitted, skipping the evidence-check rule entirely.

input: Hi, this is Ava Thompson. I'm just not satisfied with the Wireless Mouse I got and would like my money back.
failure_trap: Catches a model that guesses a specific reason code (e.g. defaulting to changed_mind) from vague dissatisfaction language instead of honestly reporting low confidence.

input: Hi, this is Ava Thompson. The Instant Pot Pressure Cooker I bought from you arrived defective and I'd like a refund.
failure_trap: Catches a model that hallucinates a product match against an unrelated catalog item instead of correctly reporting that no such item was ever sold.

ungrounded_claims: answer cites rule 5, which was not among the retrieved policy chunks

failure_trap: Encodes the documented heuristic limitation: the answer uses the rule-5 title phrase ('wrong item shipped') generically, not as a citation, and rule 5 was never retrieved - the structural check correctly (per its documented design) flags this as ungrounded even though it isn't a real hallucination; this is an accepted tradeoff, not a bug to fix.
Confirms the happy path still passes: an explicit numeric citation that matches a rule actually present in retrieval must not be flagged ungrounded.
